exchanges.question: Procedural: IR hands to the operator for the first question. No analyst question.
exchanges.answer: Opened the Q&A; no substantive content.

exchanges.question: How much did demand outpace supply for iPhone and Mac in the March quarter, and does June guidance reflect supply constraints? Separately, what does dropping net cash neutral as a formal target mean for capital return policy, and is the investment comment organic or inorganic?
exchanges.answer: Cook: March quarter constraints were primarily iPhone and to a lesser extent Mac, driven by availability of advanced nodes for SoCs; in the June quarter the majority of constraints will be on several Mac models, due to faster-than-predicted recognition of Mac mini and Mac Studio for AI and agentic tools and Mac Neo demand 'off the charts'; Mini and Studio may take several months to reach supply-demand balance. Parekh: net cash neutral served well since 2018, but cash and debt will now be evaluated independently for more optimal decisions; remains committed to returning excess cash; over $1 trillion returned since program start, over $850 billion via repurchases, plus another $100 billion buyback authorization on top of leftover capacity. Organic versus inorganic was not addressed.

exchanges.question: With the rise of AI agents and talk of an agentic smartphone, should we expect new form factors or products? Separately, is there an overarching philosophy on margins after the June quarter given components and constraints, and is 47%-48% a range Apple can stay in?
exchanges.answer: Cook declined to discuss the future road map, pointing to iPhone growth of 22% in the quarter and the strongest cycle in Apple's history. On margins, he gave the memory chronology: minimal memory impact in the December quarter; higher memory costs in March, partly offset by carry-in inventory; significantly higher memory costs embedded in June guidance, also partly offset by carry-in inventory. He gave no guidance beyond June but said Apple believes memory costs will drive an increasing impact on the business beyond June, and it will look at a range of options.

exchanges.question: How has MacBook Neo helped drive penetration with new customer segments (education, value, emerging markets) and how does this inform underpenetrated markets and the product road map? Separately, was new App Store ad inventory a notable contributor to services outperformance, and what is the ad strategy given ads coming to Maps this summer?
exchanges.answer: Cook: Apple is supply constrained on MacBook Neo; Apple 'undercalled' enthusiasm; focus is customers new to Mac and those holding old Macs, with schools such as Kansas City Public Schools switching from Chromebooks and Windows PCs. Parekh: advertising grew y/y; added ads across App Store search results; this summer in the U.S. and Canada Apple Maps will feature ads in key search and discovery moments; did not quantify the contribution of new App Store ad inventory.

exchanges.question: Given memory cost increases beyond June, will Apple prioritize share gain (not raising prices, lower-end products) or profitability? Separately, where will Apple invest or partner across the AI stack, and does this relate to the net cash comment on building infrastructure?
exchanges.answer: Cook: Apple will look at a range of options with memory costs increasing and does not want to go beyond that. On AI investment, Apple is clearly investing more, with R&D accelerating much higher than the company's growth rate, in both products and services. Parekh: AI is an important investment area, done incrementally on top of what Apple normally invests in its product road map. Partner versus internal split and infrastructure were not addressed.

exchanges.question: What levers are driving iPhone growth of 20% plus despite supply constraints and how durable is it? Separately, what advice is Cook giving John Ternus for the transition, relative to the advice Steve Jobs gave him?
exchanges.answer: Cook: the iPhone 17 family is the driver (design, performance, durability, camera, Center Stage, Apple Intelligence); double-digit growth in the majority of markets tracked; March quarter record for upgraders; U.S. customer satisfaction for the 17 family at 99%. Durability was not addressed explicitly. On the transition, Steve's advice lifted a huge burden; his advice to John is that one of the most important decisions is where to spend his time, on where the greatest benefit to the company and users lies, and never forget the North Star of making the best products that enrich lives.

exchanges.question: Is iPhone constrained in June, how is Apple securing SoC and memory supply, and is it using alternative memory sources? Separately, is services gross margin approaching a ceiling, or is there still volume leverage and lower losses in some offerings?
exchanges.answer: Cook: the primary constraint in March and June is availability of advanced nodes for SoCs, not memory; Mac mini and Mac Studio should take several months to reach balance; the majority of June constraints are on Mac (Mac mini, Mac Studio and MacBook Neo), because Apple undercalled demand; alternative memory sources were not addressed. Parekh: services includes businesses with different profitability and growth rates; the Q2 services margin rose 20bp sequentially, primarily on mix; some services are improving as they scale; hard to speculate on evolution but encouraged by trajectory.

exchanges.question: How is Apple balancing the Google collaboration and its own foundation models, and does it need to invest more? Separately, what explains the muted sequential decline in product gross margin this year (mix, FX), and what was the FX impact on gross margin?
exchanges.answer: Cook: Apple is investing more, with R&D scaled significantly y/y; the Google collaboration is going well and Apple is happy with its independent work. Parekh: products gross margin fell 200bp sequentially on seasonal loss of leverage and higher memory costs; company gross margin rose 110bp sequentially on favorable mix and lower tariff-related costs, partly offset by seasonal loss of leverage and higher memory costs; no sequential FX impact on gross margin from Q1 to Q2. Cook added that March tariffs were lower on lower volume plus a full-quarter benefit from lower IEEPA rates and the reduced Section 122 global rate, and Apple plans to reinvest any tariff refunds received into U.S. innovation and advanced manufacturing, in addition to prior commitments.

exchanges.question: What is Apple seeing in China, including any competitive advantage from rivals' supply constraints? Separately, how is the India market evolving given the iPhone base and rising middle class?
exchanges.answer: Cook: Greater China grew 33% in the first half and revenue was up 28% in the March quarter, a quarterly record, driven by iPhone; iPhone was top-selling model in urban China, Mac mini top-selling desktop and MacBook Air top-selling laptop; store traffic grew double digits. India is a huge opportunity: second largest smartphone market and third largest PC market, Apple still has a modest share, and the majority of customers across categories are new to the product. Competitor supply constraints were not addressed.
